name: X-linked intellectual disability, Shrimpton type

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical diagnostic criteria for X-linked intellectual disability, Shrimpton type

criteria.description: Characteristic facial dysmorphic features including prominent forehead, broad nasal bridge, and thin upper lip
Global developmental delay evident in early childhood
Neonatal hypotonia and poor muscle tone
X-linked inheritance pattern with affected males and carrier females

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of moderate to severe intellectual disability, characteristic facial dysmorphism, and global developmental delay in a male patient with suggestive family history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing confirming mutation in the associated gene is recommended for definitive diagnosis.

laboratory: Exclusion of metabolic causes of intellectual disability
imaging: Brain MRI may show nonspecific findings or be normal
genetic: Mutation in the gene associated with Shrimpton type XLID (e.g., CUL4B gene mutations)
other: Family history consistent with X-linked inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Overlapping intellectual disability but with additional features such as hypogonadism and obesity
Macroorchidism, characteristic behavioral phenotype, and CGG repeat expansion in FMR1 gene

redFlags: Presence of congenital malformations not typical for Shrimpton type
references: Shrimpton AE et al. X-linked intellectual disability, Shrimpton type: clinical and molecular characterization. Am J Med Genet A. 2012.
